issues.description: `protocol_lock_start` leaves the subtree root in `LockedOutside` and creates an empty `Locking(nid, nid)` range even though execution has already locked that root, so the protocol state does not represent the lock held at the end of traversal.
issues.rationale: The execution path acquires the non-stray subtree-root lock before entering the locking protocol. The transition should therefore consume `NodeState::LockedOutside`, install `NodeState::Locked`, and initialize the cursor with a range that already contains the root (`Locking(nid, nid + 1)`). Instead, the fixed head merely checks that the node remains `LockedOutside` and records `Locking(nid, nid)`. Since `locked_range` is the half-open interval `[rt, nid)`, that cursor claims no node is locked; the newly added root/state invariants are vacuous for this empty range and do not repair the abstraction mismatch. The model can consequently reason about a protocol state that lags the lock actually held by execution. The author explicitly identifies this as a fundamental error, and later PR #185 applies the exact state and range correction proposed in the comment.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus was not executed.
